quote: Collection Agency should not, in dealing with any patient under RUHS Charity Care or Financial Assistance program, use wage garnishment or liens on any real property owned by the patient
explanation: The policy tells its collection agency not to put liens on the homes of patients in its charity care or financial assistance programs. It also says it follows the California law.

quote: The ECAs that require legal or judicial process for this purpose include a lien; foreclosure on real property
explanation: This is only a definition of collection actions from federal rules. It does not say the hospital puts liens on homes of eligible patients.

quote: MCHD will forgo garnishment of wages, liens on a primary residence
explanation: The hospital says it will not put a lien on your home. This follows the law.

quote: For patients found eligible for Charity Care or Discounted Care under Adventist Health's Financial Assistance Policy, the Collection Agency may not use wage garnishments or file a lien against any real property
explanation: This sentence is a federal definition list. The policy elsewhere forbids property liens for patients who qualify for help.

quote: In no event shall a third party to which any bad debt has been sold use wage garnishment or a sale of a patient’s primary residence
explanation: The policy forbids debt buyers from selling your home to collect. Debt is only sold for patients who were not found eligible for help.

quote: The Hospital, the Collection Agency, or any other affiliate of the hospital cannot use wage garnishments or liens on primary residences as a means of collections.
explanation: The policy says nobody collecting for the hospital may put a lien on your home. This follows the law.

quote: Liens on real property are not permitted.
explanation: The lien here is a claim against a deceased patient's estate. The policy says liens on real property are not allowed.

quote: The account is sent to bad debt so a lien can be placed.
explanation: The policy sends deceased patients' accounts to collections so a lien can be placed, even when Medi Cal coverage is pending. It does not say what the lien is on, so ask whether it could reach a home of someone who qualifies for help.

quote: For patients found eligible for charity care or discounted care under Oak Valley Hospital District’s Financial Assistance Policy, the Collection Agency may not use wage garnishments or file a lien against any real property
explanation: The lien wording is a federal definition list. The policy then forbids property liens for patients who qualify for help.

quote: For patients found eligible for Charity Care or Discounted Care under Adventist Health's Financial Assistance Policy, the Collection Agency may not use wage garnishments or file a lien against any real property
explanation: This is only a definition. The policy elsewhere forbids property liens for patients who qualify for help.

quote: The following actions taken by a hospital are also considered ECAs:
explanation: This is only a list of what counts as a serious collection action. It does not say the hospital puts liens on homes of eligible patients.

quote: or the patient has more than one home, the account may be approved for legal action to include placing a lien on a home or other real estate
explanation: The policy allows a lien on real estate for any patient with more than one home, even one with income low enough to qualify for discounts. California bans property liens for patients who qualify for charity care or discounts.

quote: external collection agencies shall be authorized to file litigation, obtain judgment liens and execute upon such judgment liens
explanation: Collection agencies may get judgment liens, which can attach to a home. These start only after a patient is found ineligible or does not finish an application, but the policy never excludes eligible patients, so ask.

quote: HOH shall not, in dealing with Patients eligible for Financial Assistance, use wage garnishments or liens on any real property
explanation: The hospital will not put a lien on property of patients who qualify for financial help. This follows the law.

quote: Liens on real property are not permitted.
explanation: The lien is a claim against a deceased patient's estate. The policy says liens on real property are not allowed.
